newsitem.title: USA: Argentine megabond meets market craving for yields.
newsitem.headline: Argentine megabond meets market craving for yields.

text.p: After gobbling up Mexico's $1 billion 10-year issue last week, the market's hearty reception of Argentina's $2 billion 20-year global bond shows that the voracious appetite for emerging debt has yet to be sated, market sources said on Tuesday.
The spread, at 462.5 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, is considered tight, given Argentina's sovereign credit rating of BB-minus by Standard and Poor's and B1 by Moody's Investors Service.
Argentina initially planned a two-tranche global issue of five and 20-year maturity, and revised it Monday to a single-tranche 20-year offer.
The preference for the 20-year over five-year showed investors were hungry for yields, said Tulio Vera, a managing director of emerging market debt at Bear Stearns.
This global bond extends its dollar yield curve to 20 years from the current 10 years, although Argentina has non-dollar denominated debt out to 30 years.
Market sources estimated that the spread for the five-year issue would have been around 300 basis points.
In addition to the yield considerations, concerns about too much Argentine debt coming due in the next few years could have chilled demand for the five-year issue, Vera said.
The longer-dated debt is positive for Argentina's debt management as well as for the market, he said.

In a still segmented debt market, many Brady bond traders and investors loaded up on the Argentina FRBs as a surrogate for the five-year issue in anticipation of tight spread, said a hedge fund manager. The FRB is uncollateralized and has an average life of 5.3 years.
"The idea is that the new five-year global would make the FRB look cheap," he said.
As a result, FRBs soared to an all-time high of 89-3/8 last Thursday.

The cancellation of the five-year global did not dampen interest in FRBs, instead enhancing the attractiveness of the par and discount bonds, said Raul Elizalde, head of quantitative analysis at ING Barings.
FRBs were bid to a new high at 89-3/4, up 3/4, on Tuesday.
Argentina pars and discounts should catch up with the FRB gains and narrow the spreads with the coming 20-year global bonds, he said.
The pars and discounts, which are collaterlized with U.S. Treasuries and stigmatized as restructured loans, usually carry a premium to the eurobond, but this premium is disappearing, Elizalde said.
The 462.5 basis point spread of the 20-year bond makes the pars with 565 basis points and the discounts with 560 basis points look cheap, he said.
Judging from the reception of the recent mega global deals, the spreads could tighten by 100 to 200 basis points before a correction sets in, he predicted.
